questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the future continuous.
questions.context: Practica de futuro continuo, Quito, grado 11.

options.text: This time tomorrow she will fly to Madrid.
options.feedback: That describes the action from the start, not from the middle.

options.text: This time tomorrow she will be flying to Madrid.
options.feedback: 'Will be flying' places her in the middle of the action tomorrow.

options.text: This time tomorrow she flies to Madrid.
options.feedback: The simple present is not the future continuous form.

options.text: This time tomorrow she would flying to Madrid.
options.feedback: 'Would' cannot be followed by a gerund in this structure.

questions.explanation:
'Will be' mas gerundio describe una accion en curso en un momento futuro. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the future continuous tell us about timing?

options.text: The action will start exactly at that moment
options.feedback: The start would be described by 'will begin'.

options.text: The action will be in progress at that future moment
options.feedback: 'Will be' plus gerund marks an action ongoing at a future point.

options.text: The action finished in the past
options.feedback: The future continuous places everything ahead of the reference moment.

options.text: The action is happening now
options.feedback: The present continuous refers to the present, not the future.

questions.explanation:
El futuro continuo indica que la accion ya estara en marcha en ese punto del futuro.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'This time next year I ____ in Quito.'

options.text: will study
options.feedback: That describes a future event, not an action in progress at that moment.

options.text: am studying
options.feedback: The present continuous refers to now, not to next year.

options.text: will be studying
options.feedback: 'Will be studying' describes the ongoing state at that future moment.

options.text: studied
options.feedback: The simple past refers to a completed action before the reference.

questions.explanation:
'This time next year' exige el futuro continuo porque describe la situacion en ese momento futuro.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the future perfect correctly?

options.text: By December she will graduate from university.
options.feedback: That describes the event itself, not its completion before a point.

options.text: By December she will have graduated from university.
options.feedback: 'Will have graduated' places the completion before December.

options.text: By December she graduates from university.
options.feedback: The simple present does not express a future completed action.

options.text: By December she has graduated from university.
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to the future.

questions.explanation:
'Will have' mas participio indica que la accion estara terminada antes de un momento futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'I will finish the report tomorrow' and 'I will have finished the report by tomorrow'?

options.text: Both mean the report will be finished tomorrow evening
options.feedback: The second means completion before tomorrow, not during tomorrow.

options.text: The first is the event; the second is its completion before that moment
options.feedback: 'Will finish' is the event, 'will have finished' the prior completion.

options.text: The second refers to the past
options.feedback: The future perfect refers to a moment ahead of now.

options.text: The first implies a plan and the second a habit
options.feedback: Both forms can express plans; the difference is timing.

questions.explanation:
La primera oracion situa la accion en el momento futuro; la segunda indica que ya estara terminada.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'They ____ for two hours by the time the bus arrives.'

options.text: will have been waiting
options.feedback: 'Will have been waiting' plus 'by the time' gives the total duration before that moment.

options.text: will be waiting
options.feedback: That describes the action at the arrival moment, not the duration before it.

options.text: have been waiting
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to a future point.

options.text: are waiting
options.feedback: The present continuous refers to now.

questions.explanation:
'By the time' introduce un punto futuro, por lo que corresponde el futuro continuo con duracion.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which time expression normally goes with the future perfect?

options.text: every day
options.feedback: 'Every day' marks a habit and requires the simple present.

options.text: yesterday
options.feedback: 'Yesterday' is a past marker and requires a past tense.

options.text: now
options.feedback: 'Now' points to the present, where the present perfect applies instead.

options.text: by next June
options.feedback: 'By' plus a deadline is the classic signal of the future perfect.

questions.explanation:
'By' mas un punto temporal es el marcador caracteristico del futuro perfecto. Esta estructura se repite con otros verbos del mismo grupo.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'I will have finish the exam by then.' What is the error?

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: The base form after 'will have' is a clear error.

options.text: 'Will' must be 'would'
options.feedback: The auxiliary depends on the reference point, not on the participle.

options.text: 'Exam' must be plural
options.feedback: The noun form does not affect the verb structure.

options.text: 'Finish' must be the participle 'finished'.
options.feedback: The future perfect requires the past participle after 'will have'.

questions.explanation:
Despues de 'will have' el verbo debe estar en participo ('finished'), no en forma base.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text: 'At eight o'clock tonight, the committee will be reviewing the budget.' What will they be doing?

options.text: They will start the review exactly at eight
options.feedback: A start at eight would be 'will begin the review'.

options.text: They will be in the middle of the budget review at eight
options.feedback: 'Will be reviewing' places the action in progress at that hour.

options.text: They will have finished the review at eight
options.feedback: Completion before eight is not what the sentence says.

options.text: They will review the budget every week
options.feedback: No repetition is expressed in the text.

questions.explanation:
La oracion situa a la sesion en curso a las ocho de la noche, en el momento en que se lee el texto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses 'by the time'?

options.text: By the time the ambulance arrived, the police have controlled the traffic.
options.feedback: The present perfect cannot be placed before a past reference point.

options.text: By the time the ambulance is arriving, the police had controlled the traffic.
options.feedback: The progressive future does not fit a past reference point.

options.text: By the time the ambulance arrived, the police will have controlled the traffic.
options.feedback: The future perfect cannot refer to a moment before the reference point.

options.text: By the time the ambulance arrived, the police had already controlled the traffic.
options.feedback: 'Had already controlled' places the action before the arrival.

questions.explanation:
'By the time' introduce una clausula en pasado que fija el punto de referencia del futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'By the time we arrive, the film ____ already ____.'
questions.context: Futuro perfecto en una oracion con presente, Cuenca.

options.text: will have started
options.feedback: 'Will have started' places the beginning of the film before our arrival.

options.text: will start
options.feedback: That places the start at or after the arrival moment.

options.text: has started
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to a future arrival.

options.text: had started
options.feedback: The past perfect would require a past reference point.

questions.explanation:
Con un presente ('we arrive') el tiempo anterior se expresa en futuro perfecto. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the function of the future continuous in the sentence: 'I will be studying at eight tonight'?

options.text: It states when the action begins
options.feedback: A beginning would be expressed with 'will start studying'.

options.text: It states how long the action has lasted
options.feedback: Duration before that moment requires the future perfect continuous.

options.text: It expresses a past action
options.feedback: The whole form belongs to the future.

options.text: It describes the state of the action at that future moment
options.feedback: The continuous highlights the ongoing activity rather than its beginning.

questions.explanation:
La forma describe lo que estara haciendo el hablante en ese momento, emphasizing la continuidad de la accion.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question in the future perfect.

options.text: Will you have finished the assignment by Friday?
options.feedback: 'Will have' plus participle forms the future perfect question correctly.

options.text: Do you will have finished the assignment by Friday?
options.feedback: Auxiliaries cannot be stacked: 'do' is not used with 'will have'.

options.text: Will you have finish the assignment by Friday?
options.feedback: After 'will have' the participle 'finished' is required.

options.text: Have you will finish the assignment by Friday?
options.feedback: The order of the two auxiliaries is inverted and incorrect.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta en futuro perfecto conserva 'will have' delante del sujeto y el participio al final.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence and choose the best correction: 'She will be works at the office until five.'

options.text: She will works at the office until five.
options.feedback: That is the simple future with an incorrect third person form.

options.text: She will be work at the office until five.
options.feedback: The base form after 'will be' is the same original error.

options.text: She will be working at the office until five.
options.feedback: 'Working' is the gerund required after 'will be'.

options.text: She will being working at the office until five.
options.feedback: Two verb forms cannot be combined in that way.

questions.explanation:
El futuro continuo exige gerundio; ademas, la preposicion correcta con 'until' es 'until' y no 'till' mal aplicado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'When you arrive at the station, the train will already have left.' What does this imply?

options.text: The train will leave exactly when you arrive
options.feedback: The text places the departure before, not simultaneous with, the arrival.

options.text: The train will wait for you
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence suggests waiting.

options.text: The train will arrive after you
options.feedback: The text speaks about departure, not arrival.

options.text: The train will be gone by the time you reach the station
options.feedback: The departure is completed before the arrival reference point.

questions.explanation:
El futuro perfecto implica que la salida del tren sera un hecho consumado en el momento de la llegada.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the future perfect continuous correctly?

options.text: By midnight they will be working for twelve hours.
options.feedback: That describes the action ongoing at midnight without giving the prior duration.

options.text: By midnight they will have worked for twelve hours.
options.feedback: The future perfect simple would state the duration but not emphasise the ongoing process.

options.text: By midnight they will have been working for twelve hours.
options.feedback: 'Will have been working' plus 'for' gives the total duration up to that future point.

options.text: By midnight they have been working for twelve hours.
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to a future midnight.

questions.explanation:
El futuro perfecto continuo expresa una duracion que continuara hasta un punto futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the dialogue: 'A: What will you be doing at midnight tonight? B: I ____ my thesis.'

options.text: will probably be writing
options.feedback: 'Will be writing' answers what will be in progress at that hour.

options.text: wrote
options.feedback: The simple past refers to a completed action before the reference.

options.text: am writing
options.feedback: The present continuous refers to now, not to midnight.

options.text: have written
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to a time up to the present.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta pide la accion en curso a medianoche, por eso la respuesta va en futuro continuo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement about the future perfect is correct?

options.text: It describes a repeated action in the future
options.feedback: Repetition is expressed by 'will' plus simple present.

options.text: It refers only to events that never happen
options.feedback: The future perfect concerns expected or scheduled events.

options.text: It places an action as completed before a future reference point
options.feedback: That is exactly what the future perfect does.

options.text: It is used only in questions
options.feedback: The form appears in statements as well as in questions.

questions.explanation:
El futuro perfecto mira hacia adelante: situa una accion como completada antes de un punto futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best sentence to report what will be happening during a trip.

options.text: Next July we will be travelling through the Andes
options.feedback: 'Will be travelling' describes the ongoing activity during that period.

options.text: Next July we will travel through the Andes
options.feedback: That describes the trip as an event, not as an ongoing state.

options.text: Next July we are travelling through the Andes
options.feedback: The present continuous would suggest the trip is happening now.

options.text: Next July we travelled through the Andes
options.feedback: The simple past contradicts the future reference.

questions.explanation:
La oracion correcta emplea el futuro continuo para describing una accion en curso durante un periodo futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'By the end of the year, the government will have built twelve new schools.' What does 'will have built' express?

options.text: The construction will start before the end of the year
options.feedback: The start is not what the future perfect states.

options.text: The construction lasts all year
options.feedback: The sentence does not describe a duration of work across the whole year.

options.text: The construction will be finished before the end of the year
options.feedback: Completion is placed before the reference deadline.

options.text: The construction was finished last year
options.feedback: The reference point is ahead, not behind.

questions.explanation:
La construccion situa la terminacion de las obras antes del fin del ano. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.
